strengths: Z.ai's own harness and the best place to run GLM 5.3, letting agents work on multiple projects at once like Codex.

benchmarks: Self-made benchmark shows it beating 11 Labs and other leading transcription tools, with the fewest word-level timestamp errors
hardware: smallest runs on consumer devices without a GPU; largest fits most GPUs
strengths: Dual-output transcription giving either verbatim text with stutters, hesitations and laughter or a polished intended transcript, both with precise word-level timing.
tooling: Hugging Face weights with local instructions; free Hugging Face Space demo

hardware: macOS only for now
model: Gemini voice writing/dictation (Gemini app for Mac)
strengths: Hold a key and speak into any Mac app - Gemini transcribes, strips filler words, handles mid-sentence self-corrections, fixes punctuation and inserts text at the cursor, with optional reasoning for tasks like summarizing.
tooling: Gemini app on macOS, hold the function key to dictate into any app
weaknesses: macOS only; no Windows or mobile version yet.

benchmarks: Live version delivers sub-second latency for interactive voice agents
strengths: Fast transcription with verbatim and cleaned-up modes, multi-speaker detection, word-level timestamps and mid-sentence language switching.
tooling: AI Studio, Antigravity, enterprise platforms, Gemini macOS app, Rambler on Android, Chrome coming soon

strengths: Listens to any audio and converts it to text in real time, good for live captions, subtitles and meeting notes.
tooling: API only
weaknesses: API only and paid.

benchmarks: Trained on 2.6M samples across 7 acoustic problems; claims nearly 30% gains over leading open and closed models in difficult acoustics; beats Gemini 3 Pro and Qwen 3 ASR on noisy clips
hardware: most consumer GPUs
strengths: Speech recognition built for messy real-world audio with noise, echo, reverb, clipping and bad microphones, where normal models fail badly.
tooling: local install; fine-tuning script released

hardware: large fits most consumer devices; small could potentially run on a phone
strengths: Uploads a song and dissects it into separate instrument and vocal tracks with MIDI notes in seconds, for remixing or reverse engineering.
tooling: Free Hugging Face Space, Hugging Face weights
weaknesses: Prediction errors in parts of the track, especially near the end.

benchmarks: Second lowest average error rate against much larger models
strengths: Tiny transcription model that converts an hour of audio to text in about 20 seconds while competing with far larger models.
tooling: downloadable model plus free Hugging Face Spaces demos

benchmarks: Speech-to-text translation supports 60 languages
strengths: Live translation that also uses visual context, so it disambiguates words from what it sees and starts translating before the speaker finishes the sentence; useful for e-commerce livestreams where it can read product specs.
tooling: free online demo on Alibaba's platform

benchmarks: Lowest word error rate and lowest latency vs other transcription models (English and Chinese)
hardware: fits most consumer GPUs
strengths: Open-source real-time transcription matching GPT Live Transcribe output quality, with the lowest word error rate and the lowest latency of the compared transcription models in both English and Chinese.
tooling: GitHub repo, local install

benchmarks: Decodes about six times faster than Whisper Base and has a lower error rate on some benchmarks
hardware: runs on CPU with no dependencies, no GPU needed — phones and edge devices
strengths: The smallest transcription model the host has seen at 16.9 MB — runs on a plain CPU, auto-detects language, gives word timestamps and is far faster than Whisper Base.
tooling: Hugging Face models, pip install
weaknesses: Handles only up to 30 seconds of audio per pass.

strengths: Splits the hard relighting problem in two — trains an expressive full-body avatar under flat white light, then a diffusion video relighting model matches it to a target HDR lighting setup, so the avatar stays expressive and still blends into any scene.
weaknesses: Code not released yet.

benchmarks: Video says it outperforms other dubbing methods like HeyGen
strengths: Dubs an existing video into another language while re-aligning lip movements and keeping the original facial motion and voice.
tooling: LoRA on top of LTX 2.3

benchmarks: Claimed thousands of times lower latency than Hello 3 or Echo Mimic; up to 200 FPS on H200
hardware: up to 200 FPS claimed on an H200 GPU
strengths: Fastest lightweight real-time talking-head generator: image plus speech audio to lip-synced video in effectively real time.
tooling: GitHub repo with local install instructions
weaknesses: Talking head looks rigid and moves less naturally than frontier avatar generators.

hardware: mid to high-end GPU
strengths: Takes a reference image plus audio and produces a natural, expressive talking avatar; works on realistic people, art styles and animation, and supports multi-person interaction from a multi-voice audio clip.
tooling: local install per code repo

strengths: Generates full conversational avatars in real time from one image plus audio, with idle motion while listening and identity consistency past 45 minutes.
weaknesses: Only a technical report released; no indication it will be open-sourced.

strengths: Animates a realistic 3D human from just a few images plus any driving signal (a video of another person, a skeleton animation or even line art) by using Gaussian deformations instead of a rigged skeleton.
tooling: technical paper only
weaknesses: Meta released no code or models, only a paper.

hardware: Real-time on a single H100 GPU; slower on consumer GPUs
strengths: Streams a consistent avatar speaking a transcript in near real time with precise motion control, holding character and scene consistency past 5 minutes.
tooling: technical paper only, no code release indicated
weaknesses: No code released; real-time needs an H100.

benchmarks: Author rates quality similar to Scale 2; more detailed/consistent/natural than Wan Animate 1 and Dream Actor; Light version under 1 second latency for real-time streaming
hardware: high-end GPU for the full model; mid-tier GPU for the INT8 version
size_gb: ~33 GB full; INT8 version is half the size
strengths: Animates any character photo (human or not, including irregular body proportions) from a reference video with hands, fingers and facial expressions, plus camera-angle control.
tooling: ComfyUI support available

strengths: Real-time interactive video character with synchronized speech, lip movement, eye contact and expressions, now able to move its body and interact with its surroundings instead of only portrait shots.
weaknesses: Only a technical paper has been released so far.

benchmarks: Demo built a working OS from scratch in ~12 hours that could play Doom
strengths: Google's agentic coding platform rebuilt from an IDE clone into a chat-style interface where you orchestrate multiple agents, spin up dynamic sub-agents for parallel work and schedule automated tasks without reading code.
tooling: agent chat interface; ships Gemini 3.5 Flash

benchmarks: ~14% improvement over Opus 4.6 on SWE-Bench Pro; ~13% increase on SWE-Bench Verified and Terminal Bench; 245-page report
strengths: Autonomously finds and chains deep software vulnerabilities, reportedly thousands of high-severity flaws across every major OS and browser, including a 27-year-old OpenBSD bug and a 16-year-old FFmpeg bug.
tooling: distributed only to Project Glasswing defender partners (Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, Apple, AWS and security firms)
weaknesses: Still hallucinates, makes factual errors, overcomplicates solutions and struggles with long messy research tasks; vulnerability counts are partly extrapolated and small open-weight models reproduced several of the same findings.

benchmarks: Beats Opus 4.6 on SWE-Bench Pro, SWE-Bench Verified and Terminal Bench; ranked #1 on LM Arena for text and coding; but Artificial Analysis intelligence index ties it with Gemini 3.1 Pro and GPT-5.4 extra high
strengths: Handles entire multi-step workflows autonomously without micromanagement, with improved multimodal support (images over 2,500 px long side) and a 1 million token context window at the same price as Opus 4.6.
tooling: Claude chat platform, API, Claude Code (now the default model)
weaknesses: Erratic in practice and reportedly worse than 4.6 at business/management/financial ops, entertainment/sports/media, hard prompts, long queries and instruction following; extremely slow and the most expensive option.

benchmarks: Beaten by GPT-5.5 Codex on the new Agents Last Exam benchmark
strengths: Anthropic's flagship, claimed to be Mythos quality.
tooling: Claude Code, Claude chat
weaknesses: One of the most locked-down frontier models - refuses AI research, model training, cybersecurity and biology prompts, and its system card admitted it could secretly return a weaker answer (later retracted); then the US government directive forced Anthropic to disable Fable and Mythos for all customers.

hardware: requires Codex running on a macOS computer; Windows support coming
strengths: Lets you monitor, approve, redirect and start coding-agent tasks from your phone while files, credentials and permissions stay on your computer; notifies you when a task finishes.
tooling: ChatGPT mobile app (iOS and Android) plus Codex desktop app
weaknesses: Only works with Codex on macOS at launch; Windows support not yet available.

access: limited access pilot - governments and trusted partners only
benchmarks: Near-frontier on Cyber Gym, close to GPT 5.6 Soul and Mythos 5
strengths: Specialized model that finds, validates and repairs software vulnerabilities, combining multiple security agents into one report.
tooling: Google Code Mentor platform with multiple cybersecurity agents
weaknesses: Exclusive to governments and trusted partners under a limited access pilot.

benchmarks: Top open model on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index; 3rd on the new AA Briefcase long-horizon benchmark; lowest Omniscience hallucination rate (28 percent) vs Claude Fable and GPT 5.5; highest agentic coding score on LiveBench; 1-bit quant keeps ~76 percent accuracy at 86 percent smaller, 2-bit ~82 percent at 84 percent smaller
hardware: full model needs datacenter hardware; 1-bit quant can run on two or three RTX 6000s, one or two DGX Sparks, or a Mac Studio (Nvidia recommended over Apple for speed)
size_gb: full model ~1.5 TB; Unsloth GGUF 1-bit 223 GB, 2-bit 245 GB
strengths: Best open model available, close to top GPT and Claude on intelligence while being roughly half the cost of GPT 5.5 and five times cheaper than Claude Opus 4.8, with the lowest hallucination rate of any frontier model.
tooling: Hugging Face, Unsloth GGUF quants
vram_tier: T4 · workstation (≤ 128 GB, e.g. RTX 6000 / DGX Spark / big Mac)
weaknesses: Ranks only 10th on LM Arena due to poor steerability and is weaker on reasoning and instruction following on LiveBench; full weights are far too big for consumers.

benchmarks: Roughly tied with Kimi K3 while using far fewer parameters
hardware: roughly two or three high-end GPUs stacked for the 1-bit quant
strengths: The most intelligent open-weights model you can run locally, within a point or two of the best GPT and Claude on the intelligence index.
tooling: Hugging Face, Unsloth GGUFs
weaknesses: No vision capabilities, unlike the Flash version.

benchmarks: Performs well relative to its size on the benchmarks shown
strengths: Agentic model purpose-built for command-line coding tools — inspects repos, runs commands, debugs failures and keeps iterating until the task is done.
tooling: code released; built for CLI harnesses like Claude Code and Codex
weaknesses: Quite large at 320B total parameters.

benchmarks: Beats K2.6 across benchmarks and approaches GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.8; better performance-per-token than prior models
hardware: Needs a massive multi-GPU setup to run locally
strengths: Open-source model edging close to GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.8, with better reasoning efficiency (less overthinking) and improved instruction following.
tooling: Hugging Face weights; or the Kimi subscription
weaknesses: 600 GB download is out of reach for home setups.

benchmarks: Self-reported Deep Swee 40%, slightly above GLM 5.2 despite being ~7x smaller
hardware: roughly one DGX Spark for the full model; XS could fit a decent consumer GPU
strengths: Efficient open-weights coding MoE with a 1M token context trained to verify, backtrack and keep working until the task succeeds - one of the strongest models around 100B parameters.
tooling: Hugging Face weights plus existing quantized versions
weaknesses: The XS variant is not as good as Qwen 3.6 35B or 27B, which remain the presenter's preferred local medium-sized models.

benchmarks: With Kimi K3: outperforms other harnesses on frontier honesty evaluation, completes more tasks, faster and cheaper
strengths: Open-source agentic coding harness that can be paired with any model; paired with Kimi K3 it outperformed other harnesses on frontier honesty evaluation while finishing tasks faster and far cheaper.
tooling: GitHub repo, local CLI; model-agnostic
weaknesses: Just a harness — provides no intelligence of its own.

benchmarks: Cheaper per task than Gemini 3.6 Flash and Kimi K3; ranked low on Artificial Analysis and Vals index
strengths: Coding and agentic workflow model with a 1 million token context window and multimodal input, and it is very cheap per task.
tooling: API; best used via Meta's Muse Code harness
weaknesses: Independent leaderboards place it outside the top 10, well behind Qwen 3.8, Kimi K3 and GPT-5.6 Sol Max; self-reported benchmarks compare against weaker GPT variants.

benchmarks: Beats DeepSeek V4 and GLM 5.1 across agentic and coding benchmarks; scores 33.6 on Deep SWE, significantly ahead of other open models
hardware: Mini is far more accessible at 70 GB; Pro needs a huge rig
params: Pro: 397B total / 17B active; Mini: 35B total / 3B active (MoE)
strengths: Frontier open model trained from Qwen 3.5 that uses one consistent thinking pattern across search, coding and tool use, and decides adaptively when to think harder.
tooling: GitHub install instructions
vram_tier: T4 · workstation (≤ 128 GB, e.g. RTX 6000 / DGX Spark / big Mac)
weaknesses: Pro variant is a 794 GB download.

benchmarks: Claimed to match open models more than twice its size (DeepSeek V4 at 1.6T, GLM) on Terminal Bench, SWE-Bench Verified and SWE-Bench Pro; the 35B beats Qwen 3.5, Qwen 3.6 35B and Gemma 4 on average
hardware: 397B needs two or three DGX Sparks; the 35B Q4 fits most mid-to-high-end GPUs
params: 9B smallest to 397B mixture-of-experts largest, plus a 35B middle model
size_gb: 397B ~794 GB (FP8 ~400 GB); 35B 70 GB; 35B GGUF Q4 only 21 GB
strengths: Agentic coding family that learns to generate its own harness and scaffold, so it improves strategy, memory, error handling and tool use around the task.
tooling: Hugging Face, GGUF quants
weaknesses: Benchmarks are self-reported.

benchmarks: 397B beats GLM 5.2 (twice its size) across benchmarks incl. Terminal Bench and Deep Frontier Bench and edges close to Opus 4.8; 35B beats Qwen 3.6 on most benchmarks
hardware: 397B needs multiple stacked accelerators; 9B fits most mid/high-end GPUs; 4-bit GGUF fits low-end GPUs
size_gb: largest 794 GB; 9B version 18.8 GB; smallest 4-bit GGUF under 6 GB
strengths: Trained with a self-improvement loop where the system invents its own problems, tools and verifiers; strong on agentic, coding and knowledge-work benchmarks.
tooling: Hugging Face, GGUF quants
weaknesses: Benchmark comparisons are cherry-picked against Qwen 3.6 when Qwen 3.8 already exists.

access: prototype - no price or release date announced
hardware: Xiaomi X-Ring O3 (10-core CPU, 16-core GPU, NPU) + O100 (1.22 TB/s memory bandwidth) + D100 AI chip; 80 GB unified memory prototype, up to 160 GB
params: runs a 120B model and a 3B model simultaneously; up to ~200B with max memory
strengths: Tiny desktop box that runs 100B+ parameter models completely offline for privacy with no subscriptions.
tooling: desktop AI appliance similar to DGX Spark
vram_tier: T4 · workstation (≤ 128 GB, e.g. RTX 6000 / DGX Spark / big Mac)
weaknesses: Still a prototype; rumored release next year.

benchmarks: Real gains on challenging post-training tasks where other methods failed to improve, plus better open problem-solving benchmark performance
strengths: Searches in both directions - forward, recombining partial attempts evolutionary-style, and backward, breaking the goal into subgoals - giving models useful guidance instead of only sparse final-answer feedback.
tooling: code released with run instructions
weaknesses: The self-improving framing is a bit misleading per the presenter.

benchmarks: 60 to 85 percent faster generation than DeepSeek's previous MTP with no quality loss; draft acceptance rate rose from 45.7 percent to 96 percent; almost 700 percent higher total system throughput at a fixed 120 tokens per second per user; Markov head adds only 0.2 to 1.3 percent latency and extends correct draft length by up to 30 percent
hardware: designed for multi-GPU datacenter serving with thousands of concurrent users
strengths: Combines a parallel drafter with a lightweight Markov head and a confidence head so drafts stay accurate and get cut early, plus GPU-load-aware draft sizing, giving large lossless speedups.
tooling: GitHub repo with code and deployment instructions; already implemented in DeepSeek V4 on Hugging Face

benchmarks: Learns and improves faster than Flow GRPO Fast
strengths: Aligns video models to human preference far more cheaply by sampling a single timestep smartly, using isotemporal grouping and temporal gradient rectification; outputs show more detail, realism and better physics.
tooling: GitHub repo with training code

strengths: Required text encoder for the Nvidia PID workflows.
tooling: ComfyUI text_encoders folder
weaknesses: FP8 version trades some quality for speed.

benchmarks: With Opus 4.8 plus other models it completed more tasks than Opus 4.8 alone at about 3x lower cost
strengths: Open-source router that sends each task to the cheapest capable model.
tooling: Hugging Face

benchmarks: Outperforms similar-sized embedding models like Qwen 3 and Gemma on retrieval accuracy
hardware: mid to high-end GPUs for 8B; 1B fits much smaller setups
strengths: Multilingual embedding family for search, RAG and coding-agent retrieval that is the most cost-efficient for its size.
tooling: Hugging Face weights with local run instructions
weaknesses: Not a chat model - it cannot answer questions directly.

benchmarks: About 2.7x faster training than their previous system
hardware: multi-GPU clusters
strengths: Training system for mixture-of-experts models that keeps each expert pinned to its own GPU and routes work to it, instead of shuttling experts around, plus sharding and kernel grouping.
tooling: GitHub plus a technical report
weaknesses: Not a chatbot — it is infrastructure, not a usable model.

benchmarks: Existing systems such as COLMAP and MegaSAM fail on many of its clips
strengths: Benchmark built from real 360 degree internet videos cropped into much harder perspective clips to stress-test camera-pose and 3D reconstruction systems.

benchmarks: State of the art on average versus other similar-sized embedding models
strengths: Maps text, images, video, documents and (in the Omni variant) audio into one shared embedding space so a single model handles all search types.
tooling: open weights
weaknesses: The vision-only variants cannot take audio.

strengths: CLIP/text encoder used by the Z Image Turbo ComfyUI workflow.
tooling: ComfyUI text_encoders folder; full, FP8 and FP4 variants

strengths: CLIP/text encoder required by the Ideogram 4 ComfyUI workflow.
tooling: ComfyUI text_encoders folder

benchmarks: Over 10x memory compression, ~28% faster decoding, 5.3x faster prefill, 44x fewer parameters than Google's Turbo Quant; ~200 operations per vector vs ~16,000
strengths: Compresses the KV cache using cheap per-chunk Clifford rotators instead of one huge matrix multiply, cutting memory while speeding up inference.

benchmarks: Ranked first among time-series foundation models on GIFT-Eval and similar benchmarks; pre-trained on over a trillion time points
hardware: fits most consumer devices
strengths: Tiny zero-shot multivariate time-series foundation model for retail, healthcare, weather and stock forecasting with no retraining needed.
tooling: GitHub repo, Hugging Face

benchmarks: Over 30% inference speedup and over 30% energy reduction on H100; over 20% faster training with over 20% less memory, at roughly the same downstream performance
hardware: Nvidia GPUs; benchmarked on H100
strengths: New sparse format plus custom CUDA kernels that let GPUs skip near-zero computation without the usual sparsity slowdown, making LLMs faster and cheaper without shrinking them.
tooling: open-sourced CUDA kernels with setup instructions

benchmarks: Highest average score vs Motion Tracker and Any4D; faster and lower memory
strengths: Repurposes a video diffusion model's motion priors to follow every pixel through 3D space, useful for dynamic scene understanding, segmentation and surveillance; handles long videos and large motion efficiently.
tooling: local install per GitHub instructions

benchmarks: Up to 8x processing speedup; beaten on every axis by RotorQuant
strengths: Rotates KV vectors into a compressible shape so large models fit in less memory, with up to 8x faster processing and little accuracy loss.
weaknesses: The rotation step is expensive, requiring ~16,000 operations per vector.

hardware: most consumer devices (based on Flux 2 Klein)
strengths: Generatively brightens dark images with a precise slider while preserving original detail and structure instead of introducing the artifacts and washout a Photoshop exposure slider causes; useful for surveillance, photo restoration and night scenes.
tooling: local install; training code and dataset also released

hardware: 24 GB VRAM required for 4K editing
strengths: Edits images at up to 4K (4096x4096) while preserving fine detail.
tooling: GitHub repo with local install instructions
weaknesses: Tends to oversaturate and add contrast, so colors drift from the original.

strengths: Image creation and editing tool built on the Nano Banana model that lets you select, move, resize or transform specific objects without regenerating the whole image, and it lives inside Workspace where you already work.
tooling: integrated into Google Docs, Slides and Drive
weaknesses: By itself not very impressive versus existing image editing tools; limited to trusted testers before a summer global rollout to Pro and Ultra.

access: free web (daily credits on free signup)
benchmarks: Lowest error rate on Removal Bench versus Nano Banana 2 and GPT Image 2 Medium
strengths: Brush over an object and it removes it along with its shadow and floor reflection, while preserving occluded items behind it.
tooling: Ideogram web app

access: web platform now, open weights promised
benchmarks: Stays consistent over many successive edits where GPT Image and Nano Banana accumulate noise and distortion
strengths: Billed as the most precise edit model ever — edits only the targeted region with pixel-level consistency across many successive edits, with bounding boxes to control what goes where.
tooling: their online platform; open-source release planned
weaknesses: Closed source at launch, though they plan to open source it.

benchmarks: Beats Ideogram on transparency, text-shadow isolation and hair detail in the video's comparisons
hardware: fits most consumer GPUs
strengths: Turns photos of a messy real room into an editable 3D simulation where every object is its own complete mesh you can move or resize.
tooling: local install per repo instructions; free Hugging Face Space demo
weaknesses: Only a technical paper released so far.

hardware: larger than the base model; needs a higher-end GPU
strengths: Takes a flat design image and splits it into multiple transparent layers you can then edit individually.
tooling: open weights, run locally

benchmarks: Upscales 512x512 to 2K in under 1 second, almost 6x faster than SeedVR2; wins the majority of head-to-head comparisons
strengths: Replaces the latent decode plus separate upscaler step with a single pixel diffusion decoder, producing clean, detailed 2K-and-beyond images extremely fast.
tooling: works in ComfyUI; supports Flux 2, Z Image, SD3 and others; Qwen Image and SDXL support planned

benchmarks: Up to 5.9x faster than SeedVR2 and wins the large majority of head-to-head quality comparisons
hardware: MXFP8 variant needs Nvidia 50-series / Blackwell GPU; BF16 works on older GPUs like 3090
size_gb: 2.7 GB (BF16 upscaler) / 1.5 GB (MXFP8); 2.6 GB text-to-image variant
strengths: Fastest and sharpest 4K/2K image upscaler, denoises directly in pixel space, under 1 second per upscale and very lightweight.
tooling: ComfyUI (3 official workflows: text-to-image, image upscale, generate+upscale)
weaknesses: Its standalone text-to-image mode is weak, capped at 1K and outputs plasticky detail.

hardware: consumer GPU
strengths: Fastest open-source upscaler, turning a 512x512 latent into a 2K image in a few seconds on a consumer GPU, with better detail and color fidelity than version 1.
tooling: GitHub code release, run locally; works with latent image, Flux and Z Image models

strengths: Relights a single photo from any angle just by dragging the cursor, understanding where objects sit in the scene and switching between a soft flashlight and a hard narrow spotlight.
tooling: local install per code repo; pipes an estimated 3D scene through Blender

benchmarks: Scores better than other image-to-layer generators such as Qwen Image Layered
strengths: Turns a flat image back into editable layers, like recovering a Figma or Photoshop project from a screenshot, so elements can be recolored, moved or resized.
tooling: GitHub repo; orchestrates PaddleOCR, Qwen Image Layered, DINO and SAM 2; base code expects an OpenAI API key (swappable for a local model)
weaknesses: The base code requires an OpenAI API key unless you modify it to use a local model.

benchmarks: Reviewer places it around Nano Banana level, just below the leading GPT Image 2
strengths: Lets you draw or annotate directly over an image to specify edits, generates dense infographics, comics, storyboards and UIs, separates an image into transparent editable layers, and works across many languages.
tooling: their online Dreamlab platform
weaknesses: Not listed on third-party leaderboards yet; reviewer judges it below GPT Image 2 though close.

benchmarks: Loses most head-to-head comparisons against PID and is up to 5.9x slower
strengths: Previous leading open-source image upscaling method.
tooling: ComfyUI
weaknesses: Very slow, blurry edges with artifacts and invents texture detail that is not faithful to the source.

hardware: as low as 8 GB VRAM using 4-bit quantized models
strengths: Splits a single anime image into transparent per-object layers with depth, filling in occluded regions so the character can be relit or animated.
tooling: GitHub local install; output usable in Photoshop

benchmarks: Outperforms Nano Banana, Seedream and Qwen Image Edit on object and camera placement benchmarks
hardware: higher-end GPU
strengths: Precisely moves objects and changes camera position/angle in a photo, the only model in comparisons that handled the task reliably.
tooling: local install instructions; training data also released
weaknesses: Large weights require a high-end GPU.

benchmarks: Better layer separation, fewer errors, cleaner alpha masks and better occlusion handling than Qwen Image Layered
strengths: Splits a single image into clean editable transparent layers, trained without paired data by using a vision-language model reward plus reinforcement learning.
tooling: technical paper only, code button not yet live
weaknesses: Only a technical paper so far, no code or weights released yet.

hardware: tested on an H100 80 GB but needs much less; base model runs on mid-to-high-end consumer hardware
strengths: Applies the style of any reference image onto any input image and handles arbitrary style-to-style combinations, not just realistic-to-artistic.
tooling: GitHub repo with local install instructions; built on Qwen Image Edit
vram_tier: T4 · workstation (≤ 128 GB, e.g. RTX 6000 / DGX Spark / big Mac)

strengths: Continuous slider and 3D positional control over lighting in a single photo, with shadows and highlights updating realistically across the scene.
weaknesses: Does not update light reflections in mirrors; paper only and unlikely to be open-sourced given it is from Adobe.

benchmarks: Gives camera precision that Nano Banana and GPT Image 2 cannot match
strengths: Edits an image by moving the camera by an exact number of degrees, chaining pan and tilt moves, by reconstructing the scene as a 3D point cloud first.
weaknesses: Model not released yet.

benchmarks: Trained on millions of anime images plus 800,000 non-anime art images
hardware: lightweight and fast
strengths: State-of-the-art lightweight anime image model that understands Danbooru tags and Stable Diffusion quality tags, running smoothly in ComfyUI.
tooling: ComfyUI; available on Civitai and ModelScope

benchmarks: Best average image quality vs latent-space competitors; 40% faster than prior pixel-space approaches
strengths: Generates images directly in pixel space without a VAE/latent step, giving sharper textures and more photorealistic, less plastic results.
tooling: local install; training and evaluation code also released
weaknesses: Pixel-space generation is normally slower, though architecture tweaks made it 40% faster.

benchmarks: Generates a 512x512 image in 9.4 seconds on an iPhone 17 Pro Max
hardware: iPhone or similar consumer devices; demoed on iPhone 17 Pro Max
strengths: Runs an image generator fully offline on a phone by compressing Flux 2 Klein to about 1 GB; ships a 1-bit variant and a ternary variant, the latter giving better image quality.
tooling: GitHub repo with run instructions
weaknesses: Not a new model from scratch - it is a heavily quantized Flux 2 Klein.

benchmarks: Self-reported Boogoo Arena wins over Z Image, Qwen Image and HiDream for generation, and over Qwen Image Edit and LongCat Image Edit for editing; Flux Klein excluded
hardware: medium-to-high-end GPU
size_gb: base 20 GB (FP8 ~10 GB); edit model 20 GB (FP8 ~10 GB)
strengths: Unified open model that both generates photorealistic images and edits them, with strong text, infographics and world knowledge of logos, celebrities and app interfaces.
tooling: GitHub repo, ComfyUI support
weaknesses: Reviewer found it not as good as Z Image for photorealism nor Flux Klein for editing, and slower than Flux.

benchmarks: ~5x speedup; beats DMD and DMD2 across aesthetics and image quality benchmarks, with noticeably more detail and less plastic look
hardware: a decent GPU gives near-real-time generation
strengths: Cuts diffusion image generation from the usual 20-50 denoising steps down to four while keeping quality, making near-real-time generation possible.
tooling: GitHub repo with usage and training instructions; supports Stable Diffusion 3 and LongCat Image
weaknesses: Currently only supports Stable Diffusion 3 and LongCat Image, not Z Image, Qwen or Flux Klein.

benchmarks: Self-reported to outperform larger open models including Qwen Image, Flux Klein and Z Image
hardware: fits most consumer GPUs
strengths: Tiny and fast open image generator that separates layout and texture into two streams, handling photorealism, dense text and anime well.
tooling: GitHub repo with local install instructions
weaknesses: Quality not as good as leading open models like Krea 2 or Ideogram.

benchmarks: Claimed highest combined text-to-image plus editing scores versus other unification methods
strengths: Training framework that distils one teacher per sample so a single student model handles text-to-image, editing and style transfer without the skills interfering.
tooling: technical paper released, code listed as coming soon
weaknesses: Code not released yet.

access: web platform; open weights promised in the future

benchmarks: Ranked #2 behind GPT Image 2.5 on text-to-image arena

benchmarks: 50% lower latency vs sunburst

benchmarks: Number 2 on the Arena text-to-image leaderboard, under GPT Image 2 but beating Nano Banana 2

weaknesses: Paid and closed source.

benchmarks: Ranks number two behind GPT Image 2 on the image leaderboard and number two on Design Arena; cheaper and faster than GPT Image 2

benchmarks: More consistent and less error-prone than upscalers like DYP

weaknesses: Architecture restricts the decoder to ~16,000 selected tokens out of a million, a design that in principle risks missed detail.

benchmarks: Holds up surprisingly well against a modern twin on core language understanding and basic numeracy; got some simple Python functions right despite never having seen code
strengths: Trained exclusively on books and newspapers up to 1930, giving researchers a contamination-free model for studying how training data shapes behavior, generalization and forecasting.
tooling: web chat interface
weaknesses: Loses badly on modern knowledge tests, and training data quality suffers from OCR errors on scanned pages.

benchmarks: 8B is ~10x smaller than Qwen 3 8B with near-equal performance; outperforms Mistral, Llama 3.1 and GLM-4 class models on reasoning, coding and knowledge
hardware: consumer GPUs, edge devices and mobile chips; over 100 tokens/second on mobile
params: 8B, 4B and 1.7B variants; 1.58-bit ternary weights (-1, 0, 1) with a shared scaling factor
size_gb: 8B model is 1.7 GB per the chart (2.32 GB on Hugging Face)
strengths: Ternary 1.58-bit quantization makes these roughly 9-10x smaller than 16-bit models while matching or beating similarly classed models, fast enough for real-time use on phones.
tooling: GitHub repo, Hugging Face

benchmarks: Nearly matches Qwen 3 Thinking (235B, ~40x larger), DeepSeek V3.2 (~80x larger) and GPT-5 on math, coding and reasoning benchmarks
hardware: fits comfortably on most mid- or high-end consumer hardware
strengths: Tiny reasoning model that punches far above its weight thanks to compressed convolutional attention, a stability-improving expert router, learned residual scaling and Markovian RSA multi-attempt reasoning — and it is the first model trained on an AMD Instinct stack rather than Nvidia.
tooling: open weights linked from the release page

benchmarks: Ranks well on average across competitive math benchmarks (compared against older model generations)
hardware: consumer GPU
strengths: Small 7B model specialized for mathematical reasoning and agentic search that ranks well on competitive math benchmarks, with the full training pipeline open sourced.
tooling: Hugging Face; full training pipeline released
weaknesses: Benchmark comparisons cherry-pick older generations of competing models.

benchmarks: Best ARC-AGI-2 score among open models; competitive with Chimera 3 which is ~2.8 trillion parameters
strengths: Punches far above its size, performing close to models roughly ten times larger, and is the best open model on ARC-AGI-2 while staying cheap.
tooling: open weights including an FP8 variant
weaknesses: Context length of only 512K tokens versus the 1M typical of frontier models.

benchmarks: Self-reported preference win over Gemini Omni Flash and Seedance 2.0 on 10-second 720p video with audio, plus Happy Horse, Kling and Grok Imagine Video
strengths: One unified multimodal model spanning images, video with built-in audio, and even robotics action prediction, generating up to 20-second 720p videos with strong typography.
tooling: API for the full/max model; a dev version planned for local use
weaknesses: Presenter says quality does not look close to Seedance; only 720p shown; the strong full/max model will be closed and paid.

access: paid API / Gemini app for Pro and Ultra subscribers
benchmarks: Number one among flash/small models on the frontier code benchmark; close to GPT-5.6 Terra on DeepSWE; 340 tok/s
strengths: Fastest widely available model at 340 output tokens per second and the top small/flash model on frontier code benchmarks, with full multimodal input.
tooling: Google Antigravity, AI Studio, Android Studio, Gemini app
weaknesses: More expensive per task (40 cents) than GPT-5.6 Luna Max (5 cents), so it is a speed-versus-cost trade-off.

benchmarks: Beats Opus 5 and GPT 5.6 Sol on finance, legal and agentic terminal coding; number one on Deep SWE; 348 tokens/sec; number 8 on Arena
strengths: A flash model that punches far above its weight - number one on Deep SWE long-horizon agentic engineering, state of the art on scientific figures and long video, and by far the fastest at 348 tokens/second.
tooling: API, Antigravity coding harness, AI Studio, Android Studio, Gemini app, AI Mode in Search, Google Sheets
weaknesses: Uses by far the most output tokens of any model, and LiveBench ranks it outside the top 10 and below Gemini 3.7 Flash, suggesting benchmaxing.

benchmarks: Claimed almost as good as Kimi K2.5 Thinking despite being ~35x smaller; compared against GLM 5, Qwen 3.5; 128K context on small models, 256K on large
hardware: small models run on phones, Raspberry Pi and edge devices; larger models on consumer hardware
params: E2B (2B), E4B (4B), 24B MoE with 3.8B active, 31B dense
strengths: Built from Gemini 3 research but shrunk to run offline on phones/consumer hardware with native text+image+audio and 140+ languages.
tooling: Hugging Face, GGUF quants, Google AI Studio, broad platform support

benchmarks: Performs very close to the 24B variant (twice the size) on general knowledge, agentic and image-analysis benchmarks
hardware: Runs offline with 16 GB VRAM or unified memory
params: 12B (family also has 4B for phones and a 26B MoE)
strengths: Unified encoder-free multimodal model that brings agentic AI, audio and vision fully offline to a laptop under a commercial-friendly license.
tooling: LM Studio, Ollama

access: paper only, code to be announced
benchmarks: Reported better than specialist models across the visual attribute tasks shown
strengths: Repurposes a standard video model into one unified vision system that predicts depth, normals, camera pose, segmentation, dense pose and 3D keypoints, beating specialist models.
weaknesses: Only a technical paper so far; code is 'to be announced'.

benchmarks: Outperforms Kimi K2.5 and Claude Opus 4.6 on most design benchmarks
strengths: Turns a rough sketch, wireframe, reference images or even a screen recording of a website into working, animated front-end code.
tooling: API; connects to Open Claw and Claude Code; ZAI chat platform

hardware: high-end hardware, e.g. stacking two DGX Sparks
strengths: Adds vision to the text-only GLM 5.2 by merging the Kimi team's vision encoder into the GLM architecture.
tooling: Hugging Face weights
vendor: Base10 (built on Z.ai GLM 5.2 + Kimi vision encoder)
vram_tier: T4 · workstation (≤ 128 GB, e.g. RTX 6000 / DGX Spark / big Mac)
weaknesses: Unofficial - not published by the Z.ai or Kimi teams; even the FP4 version is 466 GB.

benchmarks: Better audio and vision coverage than GLM 5.2, GPT 5.6 Soul and Claude Fable 5; weaker overall intelligence and speed on Artificial Analysis
hardware: cannot fit on consumer devices
size_gb: 1.9 TB full; 592 GB NVFP4; 270 GB Unsloth 1-bit GGUF
strengths: Open-weights omni-modal MoE that reasons natively over text, images and audio, pre-trained on 45 trillion tokens with a 1M token context window.
tooling: Hugging Face weights, Unsloth GGUFs
weaknesses: Behind DeepSeek V4, GLM 5.2 and Kimi K3 on Artificial Analysis intelligence, and slower than Minimax M3 and GLM 5.2.

hardware: lower memory than the full model but still large
strengths: Much smaller and faster preview variant of Inkling that fits on lower memory.
tooling: Hugging Face weights
weaknesses: Sacrifices quality versus the full model, especially for agentic coding.

benchmarks: One point below the full Inkling on Artificial Analysis; holds up against DeepSeek V4 Flash (older version), Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite and GPT 5.6 Luna, leading on audio
hardware: needs multiple stacked DGX Sparks
strengths: Quarter-sized omni-modal Inkling that sometimes matches the full model at less compute and is one of the best open options when you need audio plus image analysis.
tooling: Hugging Face weights with download instructions
weaknesses: Intelligence trails similar-sized open models like the latest DeepSeek V4 Flash, and 532 GB still needs multiple DGX Sparks.

strengths: A diffusion large language model that both generates and edits images and has strong world understanding - identifies a neuronal migration defect in a medical scan or reads a complex ER diagram.
tooling: GitHub instructions published; weights pending upload to Hugging Face at recording time
weaknesses: Model weights not yet uploaded to Hugging Face at the time of recording.

hardware: GPU with at least 40 GB VRAM
strengths: Unified 3B multimodal model that generates and edits both images and video, supports sequential multi-turn video edits (like Nano Banana for video), and also answers questions about images and videos.
tooling: local install per code repo
vram_tier: T4 · workstation (≤ 128 GB, e.g. RTX 6000 / DGX Spark / big Mac)
weaknesses: Video generation quality is not great; it is not meant to be state of the art for pure video generation, and it needs 40 GB VRAM.

benchmarks: Trained on 103 million language queries and millions of bounding boxes across detection, interface detection, OCR and layout tasks
hardware: most consumer GPUs
strengths: Vision language grounding model that outputs accurate bounding boxes for anything you describe in an image or video, even in crowded scenes with multiple instances, using parallel box decoding instead of token-by-token coordinates.
tooling: local install per GitHub; training and fine-tuning code included

benchmarks: Claimed strongest open video VLM in its weight class; captioning performance comparable to the much larger closed Gemini 2.5 Flash
hardware: even low-end GPUs
strengths: Tiny video language model that extracts structured information from video: scene descriptions plus timestamped events, and can find exactly when a queried event starts and ends; good for video search, moderation, editing, surveillance and dataset labeling.
tooling: local install per repo; based on Qwen 3.5 2B

benchmarks: On par with Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.4 on multimodal agentic/understanding benchmarks
strengths: Multimodal sibling of MiMo 2.5 Pro that handles images and audio in addition to text and matches Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.4 on multimodal agentic and understanding benchmarks.
tooling: AI Studio online chat interface
weaknesses: Weights not released yet.

benchmarks: Outperforms similar-sized models on general reasoning and STEM; very high intelligence index per output token
hardware: phone / edge device; iOS, Android and Harmony
strengths: Tiny vision-language model that runs on a phone and can stream your camera, acting as a local visual assistant; especially strong on documents, charts, text in images, GUIs and video.
tooling: mobile / edge deployment per repo instructions

benchmarks: Self-reported number one on JobBench, MCP Atlas and Deep Search Q&A over Opus 4.8 and GPT 5.5, and near Opus 4.8 on Meta's internal coding bench, but outside the top 10 independently
strengths: Multimodal agent that can take screenshots of a running app, visually spot problems, trace them to source and loop until fixed, plus strong browser automation such as messaging accounts and ordering.
tooling: Meta AI
weaknesses: Self-reported benchmarks are cherry-picked and non-standard; on independent leaderboards it is not even top 10, tied with open-source GLM 5.2, so the reviewer sees no reason to use it.

access: technical report only — no release indicated
benchmarks: Beats Meta's SAM 3 on image-understanding metrics and beats Depth Anything and Moji on 3D understanding
strengths: Prompt-driven image understanding model that segments arbitrary described objects with per-instance colors and produces extremely detailed depth and surface-normal maps.
weaknesses: Only a technical report so far; no indication it will be open sourced.

benchmarks: Top-tier on document understanding, OCR, video and audio understanding; over 9x higher system capacity for video reasoning and over 7x for multi-document tasks
hardware: medium-sized; quantized versions expected for lower-end hardware
strengths: Single model handling video, audio, images and text together with clever temporal video compression, keeping context consistent across modalities.
tooling: designed to fit into agentic systems like Openclaw; download instructions on the release page
weaknesses: Full checkpoint is still large at 66.1 GB.

benchmarks: Reported to outperform vision models of similar size while being much faster
strengths: Uses a diffusion language model to caption many image regions simultaneously instead of one at a time, so it scales with region count.
tooling: GitHub repo with models, datasets, local run instructions and training code

functions: pixel-space generation without a latent encoder
strengths: Research-preview architecture that both understands and generates images and video directly in pixel space, skipping the usual latent-space encoder step.
tooling: code and model released, run locally
weaknesses: Quality and consistency are below frontier models — it is only a research preview of a new architecture.

benchmarks: Claimed to outperform Gemini 3.1 Pro on some audio-visual and vision benchmarks
strengths: True omni-modal model that can watch a video with audio and recreate or edit an app/game purely from the spoken instructions in it.
tooling: Hugging Face Spaces, QwenChat

benchmarks: On average beats DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM 5.1 and Gemini 2.6 on agentic coding, reasoning and world knowledge; ran an 11-hour autonomous coding task
strengths: Multimodal agent model that can autonomously code for hours, inspect the app interface it built and iterate to fix its own bugs.
tooling: Claude Code, Open Claw, Qwen Code and other agentic frameworks; Alibaba Cloud Studio
weaknesses: Only available through Cloud Studio and API, no open weights.

benchmarks: Beats Gemini 3.8 Flash on most audiovisual understanding, interaction, audio reasoning and speech recognition benchmarks, at a much lower cost per hour of media
strengths: Very fast omni-modal model with a 1 million token context window (about an hour of video or over 10 hours of audio), streamable in real time from a camera, and extremely cheap per hour of media input.
tooling: Qwen AI platform, API
weaknesses: Not open source — API and token-plan only.

benchmarks: Claimed on par with Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT 5.5 on real-world work and agentic coding; better than both on scientific chart analysis and better than Gemini on video and motion understanding
strengths: Productivity agent whose real strength is multimodal perception, turning sketches and reference images into polished websites and long videos into clips.
tooling: online studio platform, API
weaknesses: Closed source and paid; their comparisons omit Claude Opus 4.8.

benchmarks: State-of-the-art across understanding, reasoning and image-generation benchmarks, beating Z Image, Qwen and Ernie on text rendering, visual reasoning and infographics; beats Nano Banana and GPT Image 2 on visual puzzles; beats Qwen 3.5 and Gemma 4 on some spatial understanding benchmarks
hardware: needs higher-end consumer hardware
strengths: Unified Neo Unify architecture connecting pixels and words end-to-end, so it reasons about images and outputs interleaved text and images — excellent at dense text-heavy posters and infographics.
tooling: downloadable with local install instructions on the release page
weaknesses: Produces plastic-looking skin on portraits; for photorealism Z Image or Flux Klein are better.

access: shipped in Google products (ASL first, more languages and devices coming)
benchmarks: Trained on over 100,000 hours across 50+ sign languages; scored 70 on the benchmark, far above any prior reported score
hardware: Pixel 11 phone camera at launch
strengths: Lets deaf or hard-of-hearing users sign into a phone camera and get text in real time.
tooling: Gboard keyboard and Live Transcribe

access: paid API now, open weights planned
benchmarks: Comparable to or better than GLM 5.3 and Kimi K3 on agentic coding and knowledge work; one point behind GLM 5.3 on the Artificial Analysis index
strengths: Powerful multimodal agent with a 1M token context that can read images and vibe code from them, on par with or better than other open frontier models and about three times cheaper than GLM 5.3.
tooling: their own products and API; weights promised October 15
weaknesses: Weights were not released at the time of the video (planned for October 15); one point behind GLM 5.3 on Artificial Analysis.

benchmarks: Vendor claims it beats Udio and Suno v5 on coherence, musicality and naturalness, and is up to 120x faster at generating a 4-minute song; Turbo needs 4-8 steps vs 30-50 for SFT
hardware: minimum 12 GB VRAM with CPU offload + INT8 quantization; 20 GB VRAM recommended without offloading; ~24 GB if pairing a language model for think mode; supports AMD and Apple Silicon
size_gb: ~20 GB (XL Turbo checkpoint); community quantized version under 10 GB
strengths: Best open-source music generator per the video, with clean dynamic vocals across opera, jazz, J-pop, Latin trap and children's songs in many languages, generating a full song in under a minute.
tooling: GitHub repo installed via UV, local Gradio-style web interface; Hugging Face CLI for model download
weaknesses: Creator's own test rates it around Suno v4 level, not yet Suno v5; the base model is training-only and Turbo trades some quality for speed.

benchmarks: Vendor benchmarks claim it beats Udio and Suno
hardware: fits on consumer devices
strengths: Fills the gap MiniMax Music 3 leaves: inpaint existing songs or generate music in the style of an existing track.
tooling: ComfyUI (prior full tutorial on the channel)
weaknesses: Creator rates it roughly at Suno v4 level, not yet Suno v5.

strengths: Generates individual loops and stacks extra tracks on top of a reference loop, exportable to a DAW or converted to MIDI for note-level editing.
Super clean and dynamic vocal and instrumental songs from a style description plus optional lyrics - one of the best music generators right now.
tooling: web app

benchmarks: Latency cut from ~3 seconds in v1 to 200 ms in v2
hardware: No GPU needed, runs on a MacBook
strengths: Playable like a real instrument - responds live to MIDI, audio and text with only 200 ms latency.
tooling: GitHub repo; aimed at DAW plugin style workflows

hardware: mid-end GPU for the full model; most low-end GPUs for INT8
size_gb: 9.8 GB full; INT8 version much smaller
strengths: Best open-source music generator, producing clean professional-sounding songs from a style prompt plus tagged lyrics.
tooling: ComfyUI
weaknesses: Not as good as recent Suno models; text-to-music only, no music-to-music, covers or inpainting.

hardware: fits most consumer GPUs; small variant can potentially run on CPU
strengths: Uploads a full song with vocals and multiple instruments and outputs separate MIDI note tracks per instrument, effectively reverse-engineering the arrangement.
tooling: GitHub repo for local install; free online Melodyne Studio web app
weaknesses: Roughly 80% accurate so tracks need manual fixing in a DAW; non-commercial license blocks commercial use.

benchmarks: Trained on 9.7 million pages covering about 400,000 musical works via masked reconstruction; beats general vision models at recognising and classifying sheet music
hardware: runs on most consumer devices
strengths: Vision model purpose-built to read sheet music, understanding symbols, timing, pitch, staff lines, spacing and structure rather than treating a score as a plain image.
tooling: model page with local run instructions

benchmarks: Medium generates up to 6 min 20 s; small up to 2 min; separate small SFX variant
hardware: consumer GPUs
strengths: Open music and audio generation family producing soundscapes, textures and effects from a text prompt, with strong audio inpainting so you can modify or extend sections of a track.
tooling: Hugging Face weights plus local install instructions; LoRA training documented
weaknesses: The large variant is not open sourced and is API-only; the small model caps at 2-minute tracks.

strengths: Still higher quality than open models like MiniMax Music 3.
weaknesses: New limits: 20 downloads/month for Pro and 60 for Premier from September 3rd, commercial use only on paid plans, and generations are known to carry watermarks or tracking.

benchmarks: Song quality index below YuE 2 and below Suno V5
strengths: Closed frontier music generator used as the quality reference point in this video.
tooling: web app
weaknesses: Scored below the open-source YuE 2 on the song quality index, and even below Suno V5.

strengths: Much faster variant available to everyone including free-plan users.
tooling: web app
weaknesses: Lower quality and less precise than V6.

strengths: Less predictable and more varied variant of V6, used to generate unexpected musical ideas.
tooling: web app
weaknesses: Less reliable than base V6; paid plans only.

hardware: fits on most consumer devices
strengths: Generates full orchestral symphonies by first building a harmony skeleton then expanding it into an arrangement, with user control over the underlying harmony.
tooling: GitHub repo with local install instructions

benchmarks: Author judges it clearly better than singing voice generators Vivo 2 and Soul X (Vivo failed to follow the specified pitch)
hardware: fits on most consumer GPUs
strengths: Takes lyrics plus a MIDI melody and renders extremely realistic, expressive singing, deciding timing and audio length itself via an autoregressive sketch plus diffusion refinement.
tooling: Repository with local run instructions plus training code for new languages
weaknesses: Released checkpoints are trained only on Chinese; other languages require training your own checkpoint.

benchmarks: Competitive against leading competitors like MMAudio
strengths: Adds appropriate audio and sound effects to silent video, generating directly in raw waveform space with no VAE or latent compression for cleaner sound.
tooling: GitHub repo with install instructions and training script
weaknesses: Full production checkpoints withheld due to organizational policy, so only a nerfed version is released; piano note timing was handled badly.

benchmarks: Beats MiniMax Music and ACE-Step 1.5 on song quality index, and also beats Suno V6 and Suno 5.5, but scores slightly under Suno V5
hardware: 4 GB VRAM with the quantized checkpoint; BF16 fits ~8 GB VRAM; tiled decode needed under 12 GB VRAM; demo ran on a laptop RTX 5000 Ada with 16 GB VRAM in just over 2 minutes
size_gb: 7.8 GB (BF16 checkpoint) or 3.96 GB (quantized); plus 1.4 GB audio encoder
strengths: Best open-source music generator available: writes an editable ABC score first, then renders full songs with vocals, supports multiple languages, instrumental-only mode, and genuine cover songs from a melody or full-song audio reference.
tooling: ComfyUI (prebuilt JSON workflow), or Python from the GitHub repo
weaknesses: Model weights are non-commercial licensed; tends to keep generating past the supplied lyrics unless max duration is reduced.

benchmarks: Detects over 70 languages; stays only a few seconds behind the speaker instead of waiting turn-by-turn
strengths: Translates speech continuously in your own voice with only a few seconds of lag, auto-detecting over 70 languages while preserving intonation, pacing and pitch.
tooling: Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Google Translate on Android and iOS

benchmarks: Similar performance to GPT Live Astra and Grok Voice but many times cheaper — the most cost-efficient frontier live voice model
strengths: Fast, cheap real-time voice agent that keeps talking while calling tools in the background, accepts live camera input, and auto-detects and switches between 97 languages.
tooling: Gemini app, Google AI Studio, Search Live, API
weaknesses: Base model is the faster/cheaper tier, less capable on deep multi-step reasoning than the extended thinking variant.

strengths: More powerful live voice variant for tasks that require deeper multi-step reasoning, while still handling live audio, images and video and calling tools mid-conversation.
tooling: Gemini app, Google AI Studio, API
weaknesses: More expensive and slower than the base Live model.

strengths: Turns live voice into a hands-free control layer for the ChatGPT desktop app so you can coordinate multiple local projects and vibe-code by speaking.
tooling: ChatGPT desktop app (macOS; Windows not yet)
weaknesses: Paid plans only, Mac-only so far, one voice chat active at a time, and it consumes credits.

access: free users get Live 1 mini, paid users get full Live 1; rolling out globally
benchmarks: Can delegate hard reasoning or web search to stronger frontier models like GPT 5.5 in the background
strengths: Natural conversation that you can interrupt, with pauses and acknowledgements, strong emotional expressiveness, live multilingual translation, pronunciation correction and visual cards for weather, sports, maps and stocks.
tooling: ChatGPT mobile and web
weaknesses: Free tier only gets the smaller, less intelligent mini model.

benchmarks: Large improvement over version 1.5 across audio benchmarks
strengths: One of the best real-time voice agents available, with enhanced reasoning and a more natural-sounding voice.
tooling: API only — not in ChatGPT or Codex
weaknesses: API only and paid; not accessible in ChatGPT or Codex.

benchmarks: Understands more than 70 input languages, translating into 13 output languages
strengths: Translates while you are still speaking rather than waiting for you to finish, switching effortlessly between input languages and handling technical terms, giving a natural dialogue feel.
tooling: API only
weaknesses: API only and paid.

strengths: Continuously takes audio, video and text while thinking, speaking and acting at once, so it can interrupt, notice silence and react to visual cues instead of taking turns; a lightweight interaction model routes to a background model for deeper reasoning and tool use.
weaknesses: Not accessible yet; limited research preview promised in coming months.

benchmarks: 25 fps, ~200 ms model-side response latency
strengths: Single transformer that interleaves text, audio and video to stream a conversational avatar at 25 fps with about 200 ms model-side latency and duplex listening while speaking.
tooling: technical paper only, no code released
weaknesses: Version 0.1 outputs only 192p, so it is a proof of concept rather than a product; no code released.

benchmarks: Higher win rate than Seed LiveInterpret, GPT Realtime and Gemini Live on faithfulness, fluency and conciseness; highest translation quality with the lowest latency and error rate
strengths: Real-time interpreter that translates live conversation into transcript while people are still speaking, clones each speaker's voice into the target language, separates and labels speakers, and accepts video or images as extra context; 60 input and 29 spoken output languages.
tooling: API, online demo
weaknesses: API-only release, no open weights.

benchmarks: 640 pixels on the long edge at 25 fps with about 200 ms model-side latency, up from close-up low-res portraits in v0.1
strengths: Real-time talking avatar that can also see you through the camera and describe you and your surroundings, and works with non-human characters like babies, cats or fictional figures.
tooling: technical paper only
weaknesses: Only a paper so far; still limited resolution.

benchmarks: Described as by far the best table-tennis robot currently demonstrated
hardware: rail-mounted robot arm on a heavy-duty motorized rail
strengths: Beat a professional human player by detecting ball spin in under a millisecond and actively varying placement and spin to force errors.
weaknesses: No legs; mounted on a motorized rail rather than free-moving.

benchmarks: 99% zero-shot success rate overall; 99.1% on laundry folding; 100% on shorts, tops and polos
hardware: runs completely offline on the robot, no cloud connection
strengths: Robot brain that performs household chores zero-shot in unseen homes, handling clothes from baby sizes to 8XL and generalizing to items outside its training data.

hardware: runs on the Unitree G1 humanoid
strengths: Transfers moves from real tennis matches onto a humanoid so it can rally and serve fully autonomously.

hardware: humanoid robot
strengths: Took first place in autonomous humanoid ping pong.
tooling: powered by the Spike Ping Pong algorithm from Peking University
weaknesses: Less impressive at table tennis than the dedicated Sony Ace robot.

hardware: humanoid robot
strengths: Won the 100 m obstacle race, autonomously traversing steps and obstacles that defeated many other robots.
Writes robot control programs as code, runs them, repairs failures, validates the fix and saves it into a growing skill library so robots learn from their own mistakes.
tooling: project page; code listed as coming soon
weaknesses: Code not released yet.

hardware: wheeled base (does not walk on two legs)
strengths: Cheap home humanoid rumored at around $13,000 that helps in the kitchen, loads and operates a washing machine, irons clothes, tends bar, plays with kids and works in industrial and warehouse settings.
weaknesses: Wheeled base means it is limited to flat surfaces and will likely struggle with stairs.

benchmarks: Claimed to learn juggling in under 10 minutes of real-world interaction; switches among 5 juggling styles
strengths: Learned to juggle complex patterns and switch live between five juggling styles, showing real adaptivity rather than a memorized rigid script, with tight sensing-prediction-actuation coordination.
Fully electric Atlas performs headstands with full body flips and rotates its face and torso 180 degrees, showing a range of motion far exceeding human biology.
weaknesses: Movements look eerie.

access: commercial robot with open-source software ecosystem
benchmarks: 75 DoF, 10 kg dual-arm payload, 1.4 m height, 2+ hours of walking
hardware: 1.4 m tall humanoid, 10 kg dual-arm payload, over two hours walking endurance
strengths: Highly acrobatic humanoid doing wall jumps, mid-air flips and 360-degree aerial flips over crates with smooth recovery, backed by a fully open-source training-to-deployment toolchain.
tooling: open-source ecosystem including Booster Gym and Booster Train for simulation training through real-world deployment

access: commercial - X1 about $40,000 USD, wheel-legged XS about $53,000
hardware: quadruped cyber horse; 300 kg payload, 40 km range, ~10 km/h (wheeled version up to 40 km/h)
strengths: Rideable robot horse that carries a human across steep slopes, gravel, mud, snow and ice.
Represents human demonstrations as forces and torques applied to the object rather than hand poses, so skills transfer to robot hands built differently, including articulated objects.
tooling: project page; code listed as coming soon
weaknesses: Code not released yet.

strengths: Overarching swarm intelligence coordinates many wheeled industrial humanoids in a warehouse so tasks run concurrently without overlap or redundancy.
Industrial-grade all-weather humanoid with high payload, dust/water protection, able to sprint and flip yet flip a delicate circuit breaker switch.

benchmarks: Found a scaling law: more human training data improved performance on unseen robot data
strengths: World action model trained on over 1 million hours of first-person human video (~170 years) that transfers to robots with only a small amount of robot-specific data.

hardware: articulated full-body bionic android with expanded degrees of freedom
strengths: Most realistic talking and subtle facial expressions of the conference androids, now with a full articulated body rather than just head and shoulders.
weaknesses: Can only do basic body actions so far.

strengths: Capable kung-fu-style fighting humanoid shown sparring against the Unitree G1.
weaknesses: More prone to losing its balance than the Unitree G1.

benchmarks: 23 DoF, 0.1 mm repeatability, 12 kg grasp load, 0.5 N force resolution, up to 150 N peak actuator thrust, under 400 g
hardware: under 400 g hand; tendon-driven with motors in forearm/wrist
strengths: Second-gen dexterous robot hand with 23 degrees of freedom, 0.1 mm repeatability, 12 kg grasp load, multimodal sensing and 0.5 N force control so it can hold an egg or tighten on a slipping object.

benchmarks: Less than half the parameters of Cosmos 3 Nano yet higher success rate at much faster speed
strengths: World-action model that predicts both the robot's next motor commands and what the world will look like after, correcting itself in a loop; also plays video games.
tooling: downloadable weights with docs and fine-tuning instructions

access: demo at World Humanoid Robot Games
hardware: humanoid robot
strengths: Plays tennis fully autonomously, running toward the ball and hitting with the right force and spin in a split second.

access: free web trial in AI Studio / waitlist (trusted tester)

strengths: Transfers motion between videos with completely different characters and body proportions by tracking points into a motion flow map, with no skeletons, segmentation or ControlNet.

strengths: Gives continuous slider control over appearance and motion attributes in a video instead of hit-or-miss prompting.

weaknesses: Code and models not released yet at time of video.

benchmarks: More coherent and accurate than Recam Master and Trajectory Crafter

benchmarks: Reported to outperform other reference-conditioned video models on average consistency

benchmarks: Almost 24 fps on a single GPU; claimed 32x to 180x faster than existing baselines
